purpose: Recover explicit acronym identifier spelling variants without rewriting existing memory indexes.

design.activation: book lexical only, semantic=false and coverage=false, no CURRENT_QUERY/HISTORICAL_QUERY marker, explicit ASCII acronym boundary in original query
design.families: At most four identifier families of at most eight terms and 80 ASCII characters; preserve original form and bounded acronym/camel/spaced aliases. Do not join arbitrary ordinary words.
design.retrieval: Original exact and porter routes retained; at most one additional exact FTS phrase route, scoped before LIMIT 96; no independent OR of generic alias tokens; bounded candidate union and source-token verification.
design.ranking: Complete family matches before fragment matches, retaining other query-term coverage; prefer original form when coverage ties, followed by existing lexical order and stable ID. Activate only when a full alias phrase matches without that family's original form; this can improve an old partially matched candidate ID. When all alias hits also contain the original form, retain original output.
design.excerpts: Only actual alias matches supply additional bounded excerpt terms; original source bytes, identities and references stay unchanged.
design.compatibility: No terms/index_text/schema/index version change, no reindex, existing archives supported; recall cache version changes so old result caches cannot hide the new behavior. Non-activated queries preserve results.

known_risks: Extra scoped query and bounded body inspection may increase lookup latency
Phrase matching can be too strict
Family prioritization may suppress another query subject; coverage and original-form controls need tests
development_checks: old indexed database and cached response
